children: Singapore investors have more riding on this week's U.S. midterms than most, with eToro data showing that at 60%, their U.S. stock holdings are well above the 43% global average, says analyst Zavier Wong. It's no surprise that more than half have already adjusted or plan to adjust their portfolios based on what they expect from the election, he adds. Buying more stocks is the most common move at 35%, while 32% are adding to cash. "The vote will mostly reach them through Treasury yields," Wong says. The Fed hiked in September and held last week, and the 10-year yield has been above 5%, so the market will read the result for what it means for spending and deficits. (fabiana.negrinochoa@wsj.com)
